name: quest-count-cap
summary: Zone.exe refuses to start with more than 3000 quests. Raise the startup guard.
status: BUILT, STATICALLY VERIFIED, AND RUN: 2026-09-13 a zone loaded 3121 quests on top of mob-spawn-group-cap (build/Zone.quest.exe) and characters joined (Fiesta2026on2016 smoke stack).

max_quests.why: QUEST_DATA_HEAD.NumOfQuest is an unsigned short, and the guard compares it 16-bit ('cmp di, ax'), so only the low word of this constant is used. A value above 65535 would silently truncate; 65535 is both the field's ceiling and the point at which the guard stops guarding.

why: ZoneServer_zs_start_sink checks the quest file's header at startup and kills the process:
0x5AF12E   mov   eax, [0x1328C0C0]        ; CQuestData::m_pDataHead
0x5AF13A   movzx edi, word ptr [eax+2]    ; QUEST_DATA_HEAD.NumOfQuest (u16)
0x5AF13E   mov   eax, 0xBB8               ; 3000
0x5AF143   cmp   di, ax
0x5AF146   jbe   ok
ac_As("Too Many Quest - MAXQUEST") ; then ShineExit -- the zone does not start
THIS ONE IS A PURE SANITY GUARD. Unlike the MobHatchery spawn-group cap, nothing is sized by 3000:
- CQuestData::ReadModeRead allocates the quest body from __filelength, not from a constant
(new(4) for the 4-byte head, then array-new of filesize-4 for everything else).
- QuestData_HashDataIn reads NumOfQuest out of the head and fills STL hash_map / hash_multimap,
both of which grow themselves.
- GetQuestDataByIndex bounds the index against NumOfQuest from the head, not against 3000.
- CQuest::InitQuestBF mallocs n*32 for the PLAYER's quest array, sized on demand.
- A scan for 3000 and its derived sizes (375 = 3000 bits, 376, 3000*2, 3000*4, 2999, 3001) finds
nothing at all inside quest-named functions.
So raising the constant is the whole change: one 32-bit immediate, no relocation, no code, no
structure growth. That is why this recipe is 14 lines and the spawn-group one is 22 edits.
WHY 16384 AND NOT 65535. The guard does still catch a corrupt or truncated header, which is worth
keeping -- a garbage NumOfQuest would otherwise drive allocations and index walks. 16384 is ~5x the
2026 content (3100+) with room to grow. Raise it with --set max_quests=... if the content does.
NOT CHECKED HERE: the CLIENT. This lifts the server's refusal to boot; whether the client's own
quest handling and the per-character completed-quest state survive above 3000 is a separate
question, and worth testing before shipping content that relies on it.
